Note 3 says 'gates, barricades, or bollards' instead of 'all surface access roads' - substantively different content. Note 4 says '85,000 LB' instead of '80,000 lb' - wrong specification. Note 5 matches semantically (dumpsters/containers within 10 feet of openings/combustible walls/eaves). Note 6 says 'marked per fire code' instead of 'inspected for final approval' - different requirement. Note 7 matches.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires ~90% semantic matching for the 7 Fire Department notes. Notes 1, 5, and 7 match well (3/7 = 43%). Notes 2, 4, and 6 have technical specification errors or different requirements rather than acceptable variations. Note 3 is substantively altered with wrong content focus (gates/barriers vs roads). Overall semantic match is approximately 83-87%, below the ~90% threshold. The validation methodology states to flag as deficient when notes are 'missing, substantively altered, or semantically different from the reference.' Notes 3, 4, and 6 meet this criteria.
findings.explanation: Fire Department notes present but do not meet ~90% semantic threshold; note 3 has wrong content, note 4 has incorrect weight spec, note 6 has different requirement
findings.resolution: Revise Fire Department notes on Sheet 5 to match standard text: Note 2 should specify 'three- to six-foot setbacks from the curbline(s)'; Note 3 should reference 'all surface access roads' not gates/barricades; Note 4 should specify '80,000 lb. live-vehicle loads' not 85,000 lb; Note 6 should state 'inspected for final approval' not 'marked per fire code'. See the CoA standard notes template for exact wording.
